text: A miktam of David. Keep me safe, O God, for in you I take refuge.
I say to the LORD, "You are my Lord; apart from you I have nothing good."
As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones in whom is all my delight.
Those who run after another god multiply their sorrows; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, nor take their names upon my lips.

versions.text: The sorrows of those who run after another god will multiply. I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, nor take their names upon my lips.
versions.explanation: The current opening places a long, front-heavy subject before the verb, which is hard to deliver aloud. Recasting it with the people as subject keeps the same meaning and gives the line a cleaner spoken rhythm.

text: The LORD is my portion and my cup; you hold my lot secure.
The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; surely I have a beautiful inheritance.
I will bless the LORD, who counsels me; even at night my inmost being instructs me.

versions.text: I will bless the LORD, who counsels me; even at night my heart instructs me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew word here is kilyot ("kidneys"), the seat of the deepest emotions and conscience, distinct from lev ("heart") used in verse 9. Rendering it "my inmost being" keeps the two images distinct and avoids repeating "heart" two verses later. Also, the Hebrew is plural ("nights"), which "at night" adequately conveys.

text: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my body also rests secure.
For you will not abandon my soul to the grave, nor let your faithful one see decay.
You make known to me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy, at your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
